capabilities.name: Zod configuration validation
capabilities.summary: The config loader parses the merged configuration with FrameworkConfigSchema (Zod) before returning it.

readme.line: **Zod validation:** Configuration is validated with Zod schemas before use (`FrameworkConfigSchema`)

capabilities.name: Sandboxed plugin loading
capabilities.summary: The plugin loader runs plugins in the host process; nothing routes plugin execution through a sandbox runner.

readme.line: **No remote code execution:** Plugins run in the local environment only, in the host process and not in a sandbox (see [Known Limitations](#️-known-limitations))

capabilities.name: Docker plugin sandbox
capabilities.summary: A Docker-based plugin runner exists in the source tree but is not imported by the plugin loader or exported from the package.

readme.line: **Plugin isolation:** The plugin loader runs plugins in the host process with no sandbox, so trust plugin code before loading. Docker and gVisor sandbox runners exist in the source tree (`packages/ai/src/plugins/runtime`, with a WASM runner alongside) and are unit-tested, but the loader does not call them and the published package does not export them. There is no opt-in today

capabilities.name: gVisor plugin sandbox
capabilities.summary: A gVisor-based plugin runner exists in the source tree but is not imported by the plugin loader or exported from the package.

capabilities.name: WASM plugin sandbox
capabilities.summary: A WASM-based plugin runner exists in the source tree but nothing imports it and the runtime index does not export it.

capabilities.name: AgentRuntime model calls
capabilities.summary: AgentRuntime.execute runs its loop (memory retrieval, provider selection and fallback, telemetry) but the executor it hands to ProviderRegistry.executeWithFallback returns a fixed placeholder; no request is sent to any provider.

readme.line: **Agent runtime model calls:** `AgentRuntime.execute` does not call a model yet. It runs the loop (memory retrieval, provider selection and fallback, telemetry), but the step that asks the provider for a completion returns a fixed placeholder, so `result.output` is not model output and `result.success` does not mean a model answered. To make real calls today, pass your own executor to `ProviderRegistry.executeWithFallback`

capabilities.name: Telemetry opt-out via DCYFR_TELEMETRY_ENABLED
capabilities.summary: DCYFR_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false sets telemetry.enabled in the loaded config, but no runtime code reads that flag; AgentRuntime records telemetry to the TelemetryEngine it is given.

readme.line: **Telemetry privacy:** `AgentRuntime` records telemetry to the `TelemetryEngine` you construct and pass in. `DCYFR_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` sets `telemetry.enabled` in the loaded config, but no runtime code reads that flag yet

capabilities.name: Session trust-level tool policies
capabilities.summary: SessionManager maps full, sandboxed and readonly trust levels to tool policies; it is exported at @dcyfr/ai/session but nothing else in the package calls it, and the sandboxed level is a tool allowlist, not process isolation.

capabilities.name: Gateway input sanitization
capabilities.summary: MessageGateway runs inbound text through sanitizeInput, which strips Unicode direction overrides and flags or blocks known prompt-injection patterns; it is exported at @dcyfr/ai/gateway and nothing else in the package calls it.
